content.title: Anticoagulation for STEMI and NSTE-ACS undergoing PCI (excerpt)
content.scope: Guidance on parenteral anticoagulation in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary PCI (PPCI) and anticoagulation considerations in non-ST-elevation ACS (NSTE-ACS) undergoing angiography/PCI.

STEMI_undergoing_PPCI: Unfractionated heparin (UFH) is established as the standard/default anticoagulant of care for patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI.
Consider alternatives to UFH: enoxaparin (a low-molecular-weight heparin, LMWH) and bivalirudin (a direct thrombin inhibitor).
Fondaparinux is not recommended for patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI (based on OASIS-6).
GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors should be restricted to patients who experience thrombotic complications.
Bivalirudin_specification: Bivalirudin with a full-dose post-PCI infusion (prolonged infusion) is considered an alternative to UFH, based on trial data showing reduced composite endpoints in the bivalirudin group.
Bivalirudin is a recommended alternative particularly in patients with ACS who have a history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
NSTE-ACS_undergoing_angiography_or_PCI: Parenteral anticoagulation is recommended for patients with NSTE-ACS who are anticipated to undergo immediate or early invasive angiography/PCI.
UFH has historically been established as the anticoagulant of choice in this setting.
Meta-analyses comparing UFH with enoxaparin did not show a difference in mortality and major bleeding (as reported in the excerpt).

ATOLL.description: ATOLL (STEMI Treated With Primary Angioplasty and Intravenous Lovenox or Unfractionated Heparin) trial
ATOLL.findings: Reported a reduction in the primary endpoint at 30 days (incidence of death, complication of MI, procedure failure, or major bleeding) with enoxaparin compared with UFH in patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI.

BRIGHT-4.description: Bivalirudin with prolonged full-dose infusion during primary PCI versus Heparin Trial 4 (BRIGHT-4)
BRIGHT-4.findings: Patients randomized to either bivalirudin (with a full-dose post-PCI infusion) or UFH. Primary endpoint (composite of all-cause mortality and/or BARC type 3a–5 bleeding at 30 days) and individual components were significantly reduced in the bivalirudin group.

OASIS-6.description: The Safety and Efficacy of Fondaparinux Versus Control Therapy in Patients With ST Segment Elevation Acute Myocardial Infarction trial
OASIS-6.findings: Fondaparinux is not recommended in patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI based on the results.

trial_evidence.notes: Supplementary evidence tables are referenced for detailed trial data (not included in this excerpt).

content.summary: Parenteral anticoagulation is recommended for STEMI patients undergoing PPCI; UFH is the default choice. Enoxaparin and bivalirudin are reasonable alternatives (with trial evidence supporting benefit in certain outcomes), whereas fondaparinux is not recommended in this setting. In NSTE-ACS, parenteral anticoagulation at the time of diagnosis is recommended if immediate/early invasive strategy is anticipated, with UFH historically established as the anticoagulant of choice.
key_phrases: Unfractionated heparin (UFH) - default anticoagulant for STEMI undergoing PPCI
Bivalirudin - alternative to UFH; full-dose post-PCI infusion may reduce composite endpoints (BRIGHT-4)
Fondaparinux - not recommended for STEMI undergoing PPCI (OASIS-6)
GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors - restricted use for thrombotic complications
